title: Compliance milestone orbit matrix and control cutover playbook
creator: Sofia Martin
description: Purpose: define a repeatable milestone cadence and cutover playbook that maps compliance controls (SOC2/ISO) to engineering delivery lanes, tenant cohorts, and an evidence escrow for audit ingestion. This ticket captures the milestone "orbit" matrix (control-first vs component-first paths), the cutover decision criteria for SSO/SAML and audit-log retention, and the emergency rollback triggers. Goal: reduce audit run-time surprises, ensure staggered tenant cutovers with rollback-safe canaries, and deliver traceable proof for external auditors.
acceptance_criteria: Orbit matrix created and validated with engineering and security: control -> component mappings for all SOC2 scoping items
Cutover playbook documented with explicit canary plan, go/no-go checklist, communication templates and rollback triggers
Evidence escrow flow defined and automated to land required artifacts in the evidence bucket with TTL and immutability flags
Tenant cohort plan created (alpha/beta/ga) with dates and owners and scheduled in Console release calendar
All gating automation (drift detection + acceptance tests) implemented as pipeline checks and running in staging
updates: 2026-02-12: Initial draft of orbit matrix completed; aligned on control-first sequencing with Security; identified 14 scoped controls needing engineering changes
2026-02-19: Review with IAM/Platform; recommended splitting SSO cutover into 3 canary cohorts to reduce blast radius; Security requested hardening checklist for SAML metadata rotation
2026-02-26: Architecture sync with Serving and Console: audit-log TTL cannot be shorter than 90 days for evidentiary completeness; engineering flagged retention pipeline work (ENG-12011)
2026-03-01: Product review: approved milestone gates and owner rotation; next actions assigned to QA for gating automation and to Solutions for tenant communications templates
risks: Cross-team dependency on serving runtime (batching/kv cache) may delay audit evidence capture if kernel-level hooks are required
Tenant opt-in cadence may be slower than projected, stretching the schedule and increasing parallel support costs
Retention policy differences across cloud providers could require per-region configuration and additional QA
SSO metadata rotation edge cases can break legacy customer integrations during cutover if not covered by canary tests
